title: An update from DemandSphere on Google's goto redirects
summary: Google is wrapping organic result links in google.com/goto redirects. We outline the changes and how we have adapted to handle these new changes.
body_markdown:
Google has confirmed, on August 26, that it is rolling out` google.com/goto` redirects on organic search result links. We are also seeing them in[SERP features](https://www.demandsphere.com/platform/demandmetrics/serp-features/) as well. A result link that used to point at the landing page URL now points at` google.com/goto?url=\[hash\]` within the SERP, which then passes the click through to the proper landing page URL.


Casual users, if they are logged in, may or may not get the goto link replacement but, either way, they are not likely to notice these changes. You can easily test these by checking the SERP in your browser’s incognito mode.


A Google spokesperson described it this way: “We have a long history of deploying technical measures against evolving forms of abuse, and we regularly take steps to protect our services and users.”


We, of course, view this definition of “abuse” to be very unilaterally defined and not at all an accurate reflection of what has been repeatedly settled in the courts (in the US).


## What breaks (without our countermeasures)


Any browsing surface that reads the link in a result and treats it as the destination now receives a Google-owned wrapper with an encoded target. Where that is not handled, it surfaces as:


- Destination URLs that all resolve to google.com
- Domain matching that fails, so your own pages stop being recognized as yours
- Share of voice and competitor attribution calculated against the wrong domains
- Historical series that break on the rollout date


## The countermeasures we have deployed


We already have countermeasures deployed.


In summary:


- [Ranking data](https://www.demandsphere.com/platform/demandmetrics/rank-tracking/) for organic is unaffected
- We are in the process of rolling out these countermeasures for SERP feature URLs
- All metrics such as Share of Voice, Unified Visibility, and others continue to work as before.


If something in your reporting looks wrong, feel free to contact your Account Manager and we will investigate right away.


## Future moves expected


Google removed the[num=100 parameter](https://www.demandsphere.com/blog/google-num-100-pagination-update-from-demandsphere/) last September. Before that, JavaScript gating in the[January SERPocalypse](https://www.demandsphere.com/blog/observations-on-the-january-serppocalypse/) . Now the long-predicted goto redirects. We have a pretty good feeling on what they will do next and are already working on additional countermeasures.


We log every confirmed Google change, back to 2000, in the free[Google Algorithm and AI Search Update Tracker](https://www.demandsphere.com/research/demandsphere-radar/algorithm-update-tracker/) .
